back2basics.text: Hydropower projects generate electricity by harnessing river water flow, often requiring large dams and reservoirs. Such projects can impact local ecosystems and displace indigenous communities, raising concerns about environmental sustainability and tribal rights. Proper consultation, rehabilitation, and respect for local culture are essential to balance development with social justice.

body.label: Project details
body.text: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) is a proposed 11,200 MW hydropower dam in Arunachal Pradesh, considered India's biggest dam and a project of national importance for energy security and strategic interests.

body.label: Government perspective
body.text: The government views SUMP as crucial for Arunachal Pradesh's development, state revenue, and India's energy security, promising to respect local culture and offer an attractive rehabilitation package.

sections.heading: What is the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project and why is it important?

body.label: Opposition reasons
body.text: The Adi Ba:né Kébang United and Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum oppose the dam due to lack of proper consultation, transparency, and rehabilitation plans, fearing submersion of settlements and loss of farmland and livelihoods.

body.label: Historical context
body.text: The 45-year-old dam plan was rejected twice before being revived in 2024, and locals allege intimidation and misuse of laws against protestors, demanding a halt to pre-feasibility work and withdrawal of security forces.

body.label: Conditional acceptance
body.text: The Adi bodies are not against development but prefer smaller dams on tributaries, which they revere as sacred.

sections.heading: Why are local Adi tribal bodies opposing the dam?

body.label: Dialogue approach
body.text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah emphasized positive and constructive discussions with locals, assuring that traditions, culture, and religion will remain unharmed and that people will be taken into confidence at every stage.

body.label: Rehabilitation and respect
body.text: The government promises the most attractive rehabilitation package in India and urges local people to engage with the state government and Ministry of Home Affairs for talks.

sections.heading: How is the government addressing the concerns and what dialogue is underway?

body.label: Cooperative and infrastructure projects
body.text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced launch of development schemes worth ₹5,610.95 crore, including education, power, rural roads, and 199 projects under the Vibrant Villages Programme across 11 border districts.

body.label: Cooperative sector strengthening
body.text: Initiatives include unveiling ‘Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047’, launching an e-commerce webpage for rural products, inaugurating a foodgrain storage warehouse, and promoting women Self-Help Groups.

sections.heading: What other development initiatives are underway in Arunachal Pradesh?

body.label: Strategic location
body.text: Arunachal Pradesh shares a 1,863 km international border, including 1,226 km with China, making its security vital; the state is at the gateway to the Death Triangle, a narcotics trafficking route.

body.label: Drug control efforts
body.text: The government is committed to making Arunachal Pradesh drug-free, with successful operations like Operation Monsoon Thunder jointly with the US DEA to curb cross-border drug trafficking.

sections.heading: How does the Siang dam issue relate to national security and drug trafficking concerns?

back2basics.concept: Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Computing Education
back2basics.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as learning and problem-solving. Quantum computing uses principles of quantum mechanics to process information in ways classical computers cannot, enabling faster computation for certain problems. Education in these fields involves developing skills in programming, hardware design, and theoretical understanding to drive innovation and application in science and industry.

2026-11-22-am-aafd96690b.deck: India inaugurated its first Artificial Intelligence and Quantum University campus in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, under the National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT). This development is important for UPSC aspirants as it highlights India's focus on advanced technology education and research, relevant for science and technology and education policy topics.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about India’s first AI and Quantum University campus:
1. It was inaugurated at Acharya Nagarjuna University in Guntur.
2. The campus is managed by the Ministry of Science and Technology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the campus is managed by the National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, not the Ministry of Science and Technology.

body.label: First of its kind
body.text: The campus is India's first dedicated to Artificial Intelligence and Quantum technologies, inaugurated at Acharya Nagarjuna University in Guntur.

body.label: Focus areas
body.text: It will promote advanced education, skill development, research, and industry-oriented training in quantum computing, quantum communication, VLSI design, AI for science and engineering, chip design, embedded systems, and IoT.

body.label: Training commencement
body.text: Training programmes at the campus are set to begin from December 1, 2026.

sections.heading: What is the significance of the new AI and Quantum University campus?

body.label: State-of-the-art facilities
body.text: The campus will offer advanced laboratory facilities and industry-relevant training programmes to bridge education and practical applications.

body.label: Research and collaboration
body.text: It aims to provide research opportunities and collaborations with academic institutions and industry partners, enhancing innovation in emerging technologies.

body.label: Support from government
body.text: The Andhra Pradesh government has assured full support for the development of the institute, addressing any issues faced.

sections.heading: How will the campus strengthen technological education and research?

body.label: Human resource development
body.text: The campus will help develop skilled human resources in advanced technology domains, crucial for India’s technological progress.

body.label: Quantum mission synergy
body.text: Students can access quantum testbeds at Medha Towers and SRM University, established under the Andhra Pradesh State Quantum Mission, fostering practical learning.

body.label: Expansion of NIELIT
body.text: This campus adds to the existing NIELIT campus in Tirupati, which also focuses on semiconductor research, indicating a growing institutional emphasis on cutting-edge technology.

sections.heading: What are the broader implications for India’s technology ecosystem?
